summary: Residency egress path mismatch causing intermittent cross-region latency jitter
description: Issue summary: Customer FinSight reports intermittent p50->p99 latency jitter in eu-west after enabling strict data residency with automatic failover. Impact: Some user-facing API calls to the Redwood API show spikes from ~120ms median to >1.6s p99 for short windows (1-3 minutes) every 15-30 minutes. Environment: prod (eu-west), Dedicated/enterprise customer with residency toggle enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer routes traffic through eu-west with strict residency toggle on. 2) Run a steady load of short chat/generate requests (100rps) pinned to rw-13b-v1. 3) Observe p50/p95/p99 on Redwood Console and customer's app telemetry; spikes align with failover window events recorded in routing logs. Customer provided timestamps and sample request IDs and traces. Logs: Customer supplied trace ids: trace-eu-0001, trace-eu-0007, trace-eu-0012. Notes: Issue appears correlated with short-duration cross-region egress to us-west fallback pool and an associated rate limit on that fallback pool that manifests as queueing delays, not outright 5xx. No model-level errors observed. Temporary workaround suggested: disable strict residency failover or increase reserved capacity in eu-west while we investigate.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Ava Martinez (Support): Acknowledged. Collected customer traces and asked for sample request payloads and timestamps. CC'd SRE and Routing team.

2026-03-01 - Priya Nambiar (SRE): Initial look at routing logs shows occasional egress selection to pool 'fallback-us-west' for ~30s windows. Hypothesis: routing TTL and capacity thresholds allowed a small percentage of sessions to fall through to global fallback when eu pools reported brief saturation. Filing INT-420 for routing config audit.

2026-03-01 - Derek Shaw (Eng): Observed elevated send queue times in us-west fallback pool, not in eu-west. Queueing correlates with p99 spikes. No 5xx; streaming chunk delay increased. Asking infra to pull pod-level metrics for the us-west fallback pool.
2026-03-02 - Customer (FinSight, support rep Maya Chen): Confirmed disabling strict failover removed the spikes. Happy to run tests with controlled failover if needed.

2026-03-02 - Derek Shaw (Eng): Implemented short-term config change in staging: change fallback selection from 'any-region' to 'continent-preferred' and enabled stricter egress affinity. Will roll to prod as a targeted change subject to ops window.

2026-03-02 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Noted related alert noise from fallback pool rate-limit thresholds. Recommended adding a circuit-breaker to prevent short cross-region bursts when fallback pool latency or queue depth exceeds threshold.
investigation_notes: Checked routing decision logs for the provided timestamps: 11:12-11:14 and 11:43-11:44 UTC show 3-4% of requests routed to fallback-us-west despite eu-west capacity reporting as 'healthy' with transient 'soft-saturations'.

Examined serving-runtime metrics: no model OOMs or infra restarts in eu-west during windows. CPU/GPU utilization showed micro-bursts but averaged below threshold. Us-west fallback pool showed protracted send queue depth with normal GPU utilization but elevated networking egress queueing.
Trace analysis: traces routed to us-west show increased time in 'egress-routing' step and 'send-queue' before token generation, contributing ~700-1200ms extra latency on p99 samples.

Routing policy configuration audit (INT-420): discovered fallback policy for residency toggles had 'global-any' fallback priority and a short 15s session sticky TTL, causing session rotation into fallback after capacity rebalancing. This, combined with an aggressive routing TTL refresh, allowed oscillation.

Hypothesis: combination of (1) fallback policy 'global-any', (2) short sticky-session TTL, and (3) fallback pool transient rate-limits leads to small, periodic cross-region diversions that amplify to p99 jitter for affected requests.
Risk assessment: high for customer P1 enterprise; widespread change must be coordinated. Short-term mitigations available.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation (applied 2026-03-02): changed residency fallback selection from 'global-any' to 'continent-preferred' for requests originating in eu-west for FinSight. Increased sticky-session TTL from 15s -> 120s for residency-aware sessions. Result: observed elimination of p99 spikes during a 4-hour observation window.

Medium-term fix (planned): implement fallback circuit-breaker that blocks cross-region fallback when fallback pool queue depth or observed latency exceeds defined thresholds. Update routing policy defaults for residency strict mode to prefer same-continent fallback only.
Follow-ups created: INT-420 (routing config audit), INT-428 (fallback circuit-breaker implementation), SUP-99512 (customer follow-up verification after circuit-breaker rollout).

Customer communication: Informed FinSight of short-term mitigation and timeline for medium-term fixes. Provided recommended temporary action: increase reserved eu-west capacity if they expect higher peak loads until medium-term fix ships.
Monitoring: Added temporary alert with tags to detect any reappearance of cross-region routing for FinSight's project and to watch p95/p99 latency delta across regions for 72 hours.
Post-incident: schedule a 1:1 postmortem with Routing and SRE teams; update residency runbook with new fallback config guidance.
Status: In Progress - medium-term fixes scheduled in the upcoming sprint; short-term mitigation validated in prod for customer.
